newsitem.title: CANADA: Securities body sets Canadian 88 hearing.
newsitem.headline: Securities body sets Canadian 88 hearing.

text.p: The Ontario Securities Commission said it would hold a hearing on Friday into trading of Morrison Petroleums Ltd shares by West Central Capital Corp in the days leading up to Canadian 88 Energy Corp's takeover bid for Morrison.

"The purpose of the hearing will be to consider, among other things, whether it is in the public interest to order that trading in shares of Canadian 88 in connection with the takeover bid cease permanently or for such a period as specified by the commission," the OSC said in a statement on Thursday.

The hearing was expected to probe whether Canadian 88's relationship with West Central, a private firm associated with the Calgary-based energy company, should have been more fully disclosed in the takeover circular for Morrison shareholders.

The OSC was also expected to determine whether all Morrison stockholders should be given the opportunity to sell their shares to Canadian 88 on at least the same cash terms as those afforded to West Central prior to the bid being announced.
Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash -- up to a maximum cash portion of C$140 million -- or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
If the commission finds that the regulations were breached, it has the power to order trading of Canadian 88 stock in connection with the bid be ceased until the company amends the circular.

Friday's hearing was not expected to probe allegations of insider trading on West Central's part in the days leading up to the bid, when it made C$44 million of trades in Morrison shares to ultimately hold about eight percent of the stock.
Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval has said West Central could not have had prior knowledge of the bid because a final decision to launch it was only made on the night before, a Sunday.
West Central was the company that requested Morrison's shareholder list about two weeks before the offer was launched.

An investigation into those allegations, which was being mounted jointly by the OSC and Alberta Securities Commission, would be dealt with separately and proceedings would likely take more than a week, sources said.
Meanwhile, Canadian 88 said on Thursday it filed a challenge to Morrison's shareholder rights plan, which extends the time Morrison can search for alternatives to the bid to 60 days.
Canadian 88 also repeated it would not extend its C$652 million hostile bid for Morrison past its Friday expiry.
